- Overestimate prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values.
- Underestimate prices in the late part of the forecast horizon; adjust upward for persistent downward trends or mean reversion.
- Avoid overreacting to short-term volatility; smooth out sharp spikes in forecasted values.
- When true values show strong mean reversion, reduce forecasted values in the middle to late horizon.
- If model consistently overpredicts after a price spike, apply a downward correction multiplier (e.g., 0.95–0.98) to subsequent forecasts.
- For horizon > 10 days, apply a decay factor to recent forecast values to reduce momentum bias.
- If true values are consistently lower than forecasts, especially in the first 5–7 days, reduce forecasted values by 1–2% per day for the next 7 days.
